item.title: REPLAY: French PM speaks after crisis meeting
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday said he had asked regional authorities to impose curfews in some cities. The measures, which he said would be "partial" and "localised", are intended to protect businesses after weekend demonstrations spilled over into street violence. Lecornu also accused the "ultra-left movement" of seeking to "orchestrate deep unrest across the country" in the runup to next year's presidential election. Watch our replay. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Buildings ablaze, petrol bombs hurled at parliament: 10 visuals show chaos of Albania protests
item.description: Protests in Tirana against Prime Minister Rama have escalated, marked by violent confrontations between crowds and law enforcement. Frustrated by rampant corruption and expensive university tuition, protesters have hurled stones and petrol bombs. In reaction, police have unleashed water cannons and tear gas to control the situation, resulting in multiple injuries on both sides. International organizations are urging for an immediate peaceful resolution to the mounting tensions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Desde hace semanas, la actualidad en Pakistán ha estado dominada por un tira y afloja sobre si se permitiría al partido Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) de Imran Khan organizar una manifestación en apoyo a su líder encarcelado. Los seguidores del exjugador de críquet convertido en primer ministro han lanzado consignas para demostrar su lealtad inquebrantable. Los ministros han respondido con amenazas. En Islamabad, la capital, las autoridades han bloqueado las carreteras con más de 2000 contenedores de transporte —algunos repletos de clavos—.
